page: Google Cloud Platform n4a-standard-4 is a general-purpose virtual machine built on 64-bit ARM architecture. The instance provisions 4 dedicated vCPUs alongside 16.0 GB of main memory, yielding a 4.0 GB per core balance aligned with traditional standard enterprise profiles. It contains no dedicated GPU hardware and comes without local NVMe or solid-state storage volumes, requiring external persistent network storage for filesystem hosting and runtime state persistence.

The dedicated vCPU allocation provides consistent execution capabilities without reliance on thread sharing or CPU credit throttling models. Using modern ARM compute infrastructure delivers high hardware resource density and low power overhead, translating into cost-effective execution for continuous operational workloads. Memory capacity is evenly scaled to prevent bottlenecks across concurrent tasks that require steady memory throughput.

Operational tradeoffs revolve around architecture and storage topology. Because software must execute on the arm64 instruction set, binaries and runtime dependencies must target ARM architectures natively. Additionally, the complete absence of local disk drives necessitates network-attached storage, meaning sustained input and output performance is dictated by network disk provisioning rather than fast local bus transfers.

The server configuration is targeted at balanced cloud tasks that do not require specialized hardware accelerators. Typical implementations include containerized microservices, mid-tier web application servers, continuous integration build nodes, background asynchronous workers, and moderate database deployments.
description: Google Cloud Platform n4a-standard-4 is a general-purpose virtual instance configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs based on the 64-bit ARM architecture and 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a standard 1:4 CPU-to-memory allocation of 4.0 GB per core. The instance includes no integrated local storage, requiring network-attached persistent disks for operating system images and runtime data persistence, and operates without GPU hardware acceleration. The ARM-based design provides power-efficient compute capacity and strong resource density, offering predictable execution through dedicated CPU assignments rather than burstable or shared thread allocation. Due to the reliance on network storage and the absence of specialized x86 instruction sets or hardware accelerators, configurations must account for ARM application compatibility and external storage throughput limits. The n4a-standard-4 is suited for mid-sized general-purpose computing tasks, including containerized microservices, web application hosting, build systems, background task processing, and light database workloads.
